channel.title: AI Campaign News (AICN)
channel.description: A tracker of AI use in political campaigns, elections, and advocacy.

item.title: Democratic campaigns, organizers urge to snub AI super PAC funds
item.description: Democratic campaigns and organizers sent a letter urging candidates to reject donations from AI-aligned super PACs, specifically calling out the group Leading Future, amid concerns about the political influence of AI industry money in the 2026 midterms.

item.title: Trump pollster Fabrizio gives Republican candidates advice on how to talk about AI data centers
item.description: Trump pollster Tony Fabrizio circulated messaging guidance to Republican candidates advising them on how to frame AI data centers as a campaign issue ahead of the 2026 midterms.

item.title: 2026 midterm elections: Helping voters navigate election information in the age of AI
item.description: Microsoft published a blog post describing its efforts to help voters identify reliable election information and understand AI-generated content ahead of the 2026 U.S. midterm elections, framing the initiative as a voter-navigation resource.

item.title: AI PACs Have Dumped Nearly $1 Million Into an Obscure Senate Race
item.description: PACs affiliated with AI companies and investors have spent close to $1 million in South Dakota's reliably Republican Senate race — outspending contributions from actual state residents — as AI-aligned political money flows into the 2026 midterms.

item.title: Artificial Intelligence PACs are growing in number
item.description: Punchbowl News reports that the number of AI-focused political action committees is growing rapidly ahead of the 2026 midterms and provides a rundown of AI-related groups currently spending money in campaigns.

item.title: AI reshaping political campaigns as SC weighs whether new rules are needed
item.description: A South Carolina local news report describes how campaigns are using AI to produce content faster and at lower cost, while state lawmakers consider whether new disclosure rules are needed.

item.title: As campaign season gears up, AI-generated ads are everywhere
item.description: NPR reports that as the 2026 midterm campaign season accelerates, AI-generated political ads have become ubiquitous, with campaigns across the country deploying synthetic media content at scale.

item.title: Human-Made Ads Still Perform Better Than AI Spots, Study Finds
item.description: A study covered by Campaigns & Elections found that consumers consistently prefer human-made political ads over AI-generated ones, with human-produced spots outperforming AI spots on key preference metrics.

item.title: AI-Generated Campaign Ads Are Eroding Trust in US Elections
item.description: A Bloomberg opinion piece argues that AI-generated campaign ads are undermining voter trust in U.S. elections and calls for stronger regulatory safeguards around their use.

item.title: KEN PAXTON BS AI Campaign Ad Features a Fake James Talarico Misquoting Himself
item.description: Ken Paxton's campaign released an AI-generated ad that depicts his opponent James Talarico appearing to misquote himself, fabricating a statement Talarico never made.

item.title: Rep . Lorena Austin troubled by Turning Point united states deepfakes
item.description: Turning Point USA activists posted a deepfake video showing Arizona Rep. Lorena Austin planting a "Democratas Por Biggs" sign in downtown Mesa, which Austin described as troubling.

item.title: Sunday Edition : Slopping Towards Bethlehem
item.description: Republican State Senator Michael Lee's campaign in North Carolina released an AI deepfake ad mocking his Democratic opponent Jessica Bichler; the piece examines the ad in the context of AI-generated political content becoming routine and some states moving to regulate it.

item.title: The Information Environment Has Changed. Has Your Campaign?
item.description: A Campaigns & Elections practitioner column argues that voters now increasingly encounter politics through AI-generated answers in search results and social feeds, and urges campaign digital teams to rethink content strategy to reach audiences in those new channels.

item.title: Campaigns Use AI Despite ChatGPT Ban
item.description: Major-party candidates in the 2026 midterms are acknowledging in campaign filings and website fine print that they are using AI — including tools subject to ChatGPT's election-use restrictions — to reach voters, according to a report aggregated by Political Wire.

item.title: Pro - Paramount Group Uses AI to Pressure Bonta to Drop Antitrust Case
item.description: An advocacy group called Neighbors for Strong Communities, which supports the Paramount-Warner Bros. merger, is using an AI platform called Influent AI to help people generate and send personalized messages urging California Attorney General Rob Bonta to drop his antitrust lawsuit against the deal.

item.title: Paid actors, AI writing: How a new kind of video business cashed in on America's divided politics
item.description: Semafor reports that 'ghost creator' networks are producing large volumes of nearly identical partisan political videos using paid actors and AI-written scripts, reaching millions of viewers with sensationalized content targeting Democrats.

item.title: Synthetic Everything Hits The Campaign Trail
item.description: Campaign Trend reports on a wave of synthetic AI-generated content in the 2026 campaign cycle, citing Cory Booker's TikTok presence and alleged forged donations in Arizona as illustrative cases of AI-synthetic tactics entering campaign operations.

item.title: Democrats Are Getting Some Answers to Their Chatbot Problems
item.description: New research from a Democratic-aligned firm estimates AI chatbots receive about 650,000 political questions weekly, and Democrats are working to address problems with how those chatbots respond to campaign-related queries.

item.title: Announcing HGL’s Agentic AI Open Call Investments
item.description: Higher Ground Labs announced investments in five companies — Baraza, Context, Haystack, Locunity, and Revere — through its Agentic AI Open Call, backing startups building agentic AI tools for progressive political campaigns.

item.title: Exclusive: Meta disrupts Iran-linked AI operation targeting politicians, journalists
item.description: Meta says it identified and disrupted an Iran-linked influence operation that used AI-generated content to target politicians and journalists on Facebook and Instagram.

item.title: NGP VAN Wants Campaigns to Chat With Its CRM
item.description: NGP VAN has launched Navigator, a natural-language AI feature built into its CRM that allows campaign staffers to query their voter and donor databases conversationally instead of through traditional search interfaces.

item.title: Michigan Congressional Candidate Says Viral Clip of His Voice Is a ‘Fabrication’
item.description: Michigan congressional Democratic nominee Jeremy Moss is publicly contesting a viral audio clip of his voice, calling it a manipulated fabrication that "peddles in offensive tropes and lies."

item.title: Here Come the Synthetic Voters
item.description: TechPolicy.Press spoke with two experts about the growing use of AI-generated synthetic voters as substitutes for human focus groups in campaigns, describing the phenomenon as something campaigns will soon encounter if they haven't already.

item.title: The new kingmakers: Crypto, AI and betting firms fuel record spending on the 2026 midterms
item.description: A Reuters report finds that AI companies and their billionaire backers are among the top spenders in the 2026 U.S. midterm elections, joining crypto and prediction-market firms as newly dominant forces in campaign finance, displacing traditional corporate power brokers.

item.title: What To Know Before You Vibecode Your Own Campaign Software
item.description: Campaign Trend published a practitioner guide on using AI-assisted 'vibe coding' to build custom campaign software, advising that projects should be kept small and isolated from sensitive data to stay focused on election-winning work.

item.title: AI Campaign Insights Sessions – Newest Capability Powered by AI Agent Bayes
item.description: Upwave, a brand outcomes measurement platform, launched AI Campaign Insights Sessions, a new capability within its AI agent Bayes that gives marketers 24/7 on-demand access to explore campaign performance data and methodology through live AI interaction.

item.title: Grassroots Analytics is Acquiring Quiller AI
item.description: Grassroots Analytics announced it is acquiring Quiller AI, a generative AI fundraising tool, with the goal of integrating Quiller's AI copywriting capabilities into Grassroots Analytics' progressive donor data and segmentation platform to create an all-in-one AI fundraising product.

item.title: States rush to police AI deepfakes ahead of midterm elections
item.description: Marketplace reported that states are accelerating efforts to regulate AI-generated deepfakes in political content ahead of the 2026 midterm elections, reflecting a broader push to address synthetic media in campaigns before November.

item.title: AI Becomes a Major Election Issue for the First Time
item.description: Political Wire flags a Washington Post report finding that hundreds of House, Senate, and gubernatorial candidates are actively engaging with AI as a campaign issue, with AI and data centers appearing on more candidate websites than Israel or manufacturing. The piece frames 2026 as the first election cycle in which AI has featured widely as a political issue rather than merely a campaign tool.

item.title: Q&A: California’s Top Politics Watchdog on AI and Influencers
item.description: Campaigns & Elections published a Q&A with California Fair Political Practices Commission Chair Adam Silver exploring how the agency is thinking about AI-generated political content and influencer disclosures, including the tension between free speech and campaign finance regulation. Silver addresses what the FPPC is watching and how it may act on new campaign technology frontiers.
